speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, please tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if the pain is relieved by passing stool.

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the relief of pain with defecation and mucus are very specific. To determine if this is inflammatory bowel disease or an infection like Giardia from your camping trip, have you noticed any blood in your stool, fever, or unintended weight loss? Please also tell me if you have had any similar episodes in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D). The presence of mucus, urgency, and pain relief with defecation, combined with the absence of alarm symptoms like blood or weight loss, strongly points to IBS rather than an infectious etiology or inflammatory bowel disease.
